nonLabourLines.description: Stripe integration sandbox/testing fees and PCI compliance review
Legacy Oracle data migration tooling / temporary read-replica licensing
Staging/CI cloud infrastructure setup (compute, storage) for 3 months
Contingency for third-party/API rate-limit or webhook debugging

assumptions: No historical actuals (real spend data) exist for this project; estimate is based on backlog points, task descriptions, and standard delivery ratios rather than observed velocity.
1 story point ≈ 6-7 hours of blended effort, adjusted per task complexity and role mix (e.g. migration and payment integration weighted heavier per point due to risk).

Backend Developer (1.5 FTE = ~240 hrs/month capacity) is the primary bottleneck given RBAC, payments, and migration all need heavy backend work; allocated hours reflect near-full utilization across an assumed ~3.5 month timeline.
Frontend Developer (1.0 FTE) hours cover component library, dashboard, invoice UI, and RBAC UI enforcement.

QA Engineer at 0.6 FTE is thinly staffed relative to 8 backlog items spanning auth, payments, RBAC and migration; QA hours are concentrated on Urgent/High risk items (auth, payments, migration validation) and may need to be supplemented or timeline extended.
DevOps Engineer at 0.4 FTE covers CI/staging setup (PW-1) plus ongoing pipeline support; allocation is deliberately light and front-loaded early in the project.
Legacy data migration (PW-8, 21 points) is treated as the highest-effort item due to volume (400k records, 2M invoice lines) and reconciliation/validation needs, with extra non-labour tooling cost.
Payment provider integration (PW-7) includes webhook handling and reconciliation logic, assumed to require both backend and QA effort plus a PCI/compliance review line item.
Design system (PW-2) is Medium priority and scoped conservatively as a reusable component set rather than a full design language system.
Estimate assumes no major scope changes, stable requirements, and availability of a Stripe sandbox and legacy Oracle DB access from project start.
Timeline assumed at roughly 14-16 weeks based on available FTE capacity against total backlog points (81 points).
input.reasoning: Backlog totals 81 story points across 8 tasks. Using a blended ~6-7 hours/point (higher for the migration and payment items due to integration/reconciliation risk, lower for well-understood CRUD-style UI work), total effort was distributed across the four staffed roles in proportion to their FTE capacity and the nature of the work: Backend Developer carries the largest share (auth, RBAC, payments, migration all need API/service work), Frontend Developer covers the design system and all UI-facing tasks, QA Engineer effort is concentrated on the highest-risk/Urgent items given its limited 0.6 FTE capacity, and DevOps Engineer effort is front-loaded on CI/staging setup with light ongoing support. Non-labour costs cover Stripe/PCI review, migration tooling, cloud/staging infrastructure, and a contingency buffer for third-party integration friction. The Most Likely scenario sums labour (~172,430) plus non-labour (~18,500) plus ~8-9% schedule/scope contingency baked into the pessimistic case; optimistic assumes tighter scope realization and no migration surprises, pessimistic assumes QA understaffing and migration/webhook issues extend timeline and require rate-card overtime-equivalent hours. Priority breakdown is apportioned by summing task-level effort estimates (weighted by points and complexity) per priority bucket, converted at blended labour cost.

reductions.description: Descope Legacy Data Migration (PW-8) to a phased approach: migrate customer records now, defer 2M invoice-line historical migration to a post-launch phase.
reductions.effect: Reduces Backend Developer and QA hours tied to migration validation in this phase; invoice history remains available in legacy system in read-only mode until phase 2.

reductions.description: Reduce Design System (PW-2) scope to only the components strictly needed for PW-3/PW-5/PW-6 (buttons, forms, tables) and defer full theming/dialog polish.
reductions.effect: Cuts ~80 Frontend Developer hours; theming tokens and dialog components can be added incrementally as later tasks require them.

reductions.description: Defer full RBAC per-project permission matrix (PW-4) UI enforcement to a fast-follow release, shipping API-level enforcement only at launch.
reductions.effect: Removes ~70 Frontend Developer and ~30 Backend Developer hours from initial scope; acceptable since API-level checks still secure the system.

reductions.description: Reduce DevOps non-labour infrastructure spend by using a shared/lower-tier staging environment instead of dedicated cloud resources.
reductions.effect: Lowers the staging/CI infrastructure line item; slightly slower staging performance is an acceptable tradeoff pre-launch.

reductions.description: Narrow Payment Provider Integration (PW-7) initial scope to card payments only, deferring reconciliation automation to a manual/semi-manual process for the first release.
reductions.effect: Cuts ~50 Backend Developer and ~20 QA hours; finance team handles reconciliation manually short-term, automation added later.
